answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because ivory only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, orchard is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any meadow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
